$comment: Venue steward registry — DATA, not code.
One entry per venue that has a steward. Adding a venue means adding a
row here; it never means a new branch anywhere in the steward. That is the
whole point: when a venue moves to its own node, you change `endpoint` and
nothing else.
Co-located stewards currently listen on this machine. That is a
deployment fact recorded in one field, not an architectural one — the
steward never in-process-calls a venue steward and never imports one.
authority: what this steward is allowed to assert. A venue steward may
only speak for its own venueId (enforced at intake, and the registry is
what makes that check possible while they are co-located).
'suggest' may file listings but may not assert urgency or choose a tier.
No entry may grant any authority over another venue.

ven_common_room.name: The Common Room
ven_common_room.note: Reading room + music. First venue steward, co-located for now.

$comment: Personal stewards are readers' own agents. They reach the same intake
with a different authority: they may SUGGEST a listing, never assert one
on a venue's behalf. A personal steward is not in `venues` because it has
no venue authority at all — which is exactly why it cannot impersonate
one.
Known personal stewards, by the reader's chosen handle. Unlisted
handles are still accepted; they simply land as 'unregistered' and are
held rather than listed.

handle:operator.note: The reader. May file notes and suggestions against their own calendar.

$comment: Invariants that hold for every caller regardless of entry above.
These are refused at intake and never granted by configuration.
refusedRationale: A submission cannot assert urgency, and cannot set its own tier or rail.
Whether anything reaches a reader is the steward's decision, made from the
reader's own history — not from the sender's claim. A venue steward is a
first-party source about its OWN venue and that authority is real; it
does not extend to interrupting anybody.
